jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Intelligent Computing Architectures
jobs.description:
The Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a one-year postdoctoral researcher position within Intelligent Computing Architectures, focusing on Hardware-Aware Quantum Machine Learning. The appointment runs for one year from March 1, 2027, with the possibility of extension subject to available funding.

We are seeking a highly motivated candidate to design, optimize, and evaluate hybrid quantum-classical learning systems under realistic hardware constraints. The project is platform-independent and will investigate how noise, limited quantum resources, device connectivity, and classical computational overhead affect learning performance and practical implementation.

Possible research directions include hardware-aware model design and training, quantum-classical ensemble learning and mixture-of-experts, resource-efficient learning methods, and automated architecture search. The specific research programme will be defined with the successful applicant according to their expertise and the project objectives, with a focused and achievable scope for the initial year. Evaluation will include suitable classical baselines and explicit assessment of computational resource requirements.

The successful candidate will work on model design, quantum programming, simulation, training, and experimental evaluation of hybrid quantum-classical learning systems. The position includes collaboration with academic, industrial, and technology-development partners, identifying relevant research and implementation opportunities, and supporting joint activities. The candidate will also contribute to research proposals and funding applications related to quantum machine learning, intelligent computing architectures, and resource-efficient computing, as well as publications, technical documentation, and project reporting. The research will be supervised by Assistant Professor Alberto Marchisio.

 

As a Postdoc in Hardware-Aware Quantum Machine Learning, your key responsibilities will be to:

• 
Design, implement, and simulate hybrid quantum-classical learning models, investigating the effects of noise, connectivity, finite sampling, resource limitations, and training conditions. Explore suitable methods such as hardware-aware training, ensemble learning, mixture-of-experts, or architecture search within the agreed research program.

• 
Conduct reproducible experimental evaluations of learning performance, trainability, noise resilience, and computational resource requirements using quantum programming frameworks and machine learning tools. Compare results with suitable classical baselines and correlate observed behavior with model design and hardware constraints.

• 
Support collaboration with Danish and international academic, industrial, and technology-development partners in quantum machine learning and intelligent computing architectures, identify relevant research and implementation opportunities, contribute to joint activities, and prepare research proposals, funding applications, publications, technical documentation, and project reports.

 

What we offer 

• 
A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing section integrating expertise in analog/digital IC design, spintronics, advanced computing, semiconductor technologies, and energy-efficient system architectures. 

• 
An opportunity to develop a platform-independent research program in hardware-aware quantum machine learning, combining quantum programming, simulation, and machine learning methods with resource-aware evaluation.

• 
Opportunities for collaboration across SDU and with national and international academic and industrial partners in quantum machine learning, microelectronics, AI accelerators, and advanced computing.

• 
Strong support for professional development through the Lecturer Training Programme and mentoring, as well as opportunities to develop experience in research proposal writing, project development, and collaboration with Danish and European technology partners. 

• 
An open and collaborative research culture within SDU’s Faculty of Engineering (TEK), at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME), supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, computing architectures, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence.

 

What we expect 

Applicants should hold a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Quantum Computing, Machine Learning, or a closely related field (the degree should have been completed within the last 6 years at most): 

• 
Demonstrated experience in quantum programming using frameworks such as Qiskit, PennyLane, or equivalent tools, including implementation and simulation of quantum circuits.

• 
Demonstrated experience in machine learning, including model implementation, training, and evaluation, with strong programming skills. Experience in quantum machine learning, hybrid quantum-classical models, noise-aware optimization, ensemble methods, or automated architecture search is an advantage.

• 
A strong research track record demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications and the ability to work effectively in collaborative research environments. Experience in writing research proposals, funding applications, or project plans is highly desirable.

• 
Team player with strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with academic, industrial, and technology-development partners across Denmark and Europe. 

All candidates must demonstrate excellent verbal and written English skills, along with very good communication abilities and the ability to communicate technical results to multidisciplinary and international partners. 

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). The section conducts internationally recognized research in integrated circuits, semiconductor technologies, spintronics, photonics, and advanced computing, and plays a central role in SDU’s ambition to be a national and European hub for semiconductor and chip innovation. The postdoc will work with Assistant Professor Alberto Marchisio on hardware-aware quantum machine learning, with opportunities to connect this research to the section’s expertise in AI accelerators and energy-efficient computing architectures.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Odense. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the research and the position, please contact Assistant Professor Alberto Marchisio (chisio@sdu.dk), research contact and supervisor. Additional enquiries may be directed to Professor Farshad Moradi (moradi@sdu.dk), Head of the SDU Microelectronics section. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is December 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial one-year period, and the preferred start date is from March 1, 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Assistant professor in quantum mathematics
jobs.description:
The position
The Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), seeks outstanding candidates to fill a number of 3-year assistant professor positions in Quantum Mathematics with emphasis on pure mathematics with relations to quantum theory.
The targeted starting date of the position is 01.08.2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

About the Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM)
Over the past seven years, QM has built a highly international and interdisciplinary research environment spanning a broad spectrum of pure mathematics, mathematical physics and quantum computer science. The Centre has attracted leading international researchers to Odense and developed a unique research environment spanning both fundamental and applied research.

The University of Southern Denmark has recently invested DKK 50 million in the Centre for Quantum Mathematics, on top of its continuous substantial basic funding of the centre, which will enable the Centre to further expand its scientific capacity, attract and retain leading international researchers, increase the acquisition of competitive external research funding and establish strategic collaborations with industry, public authorities and international partners.

As part of this continued development and expansion, QM will move into a new dedicated building from next year. The new building will be located on the SDU campus in Odense and will provide a dedicated research environment for the Centre and its growing international research community.

Research activities and funding
The QM centre is located at the Faculty of Science on the international campus in Odense, Denmark and it is hosting several large European, Danish and American grants including “New Structures in Low-Dimensional Topology” (Simons Collaboration) & “Topological Photonic Quantum Computing and its Applications” (Innovation Fund Denmark) both led by PI and Centre Director Jørgen Ellegaard Andersen; “Mathematics of the open topological string” (VILLUM Investigator) led by Professor Vivek Shende; “The Quantum Geometry of Dynamical Systems” (VILLUM Ascending Investigator) and “The Emergent Geometry of Categories” (DFF Sapere Aude) both led by Associate Professor Fabian Haiden; “New invariants in low-dimensional topology via quantum field theory” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Associate Professor Du Pei, “Global Categorical Symmetries and Phases of Quantum Matter” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Assistant Professor Apoorv Tiwari, “From Pertubative to Non-pertubative Quantum Field Theory by cutting and gluing” (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Assistant Professor Konstantin Wernli and finally “Leveraging Algebraic Geometry for High-Precision Fundamental Physics“ (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Associate Professor Matthias Wilhelm.

Job description
A successful candidate will drive internationally competitive research, collaborate with the world community in the field, and attract competitive external research funding. The candidates are expected to contribute significantly to QM’s excellent research and teaching environment and to provide outstanding education. The candidates will get the opportunity to shape this development together with the team and implement research project ideas with national and international impact. 

Topics of interest: Algebra, algebraic geometry, differential geometry, algebraic topology, complex geometry, quantum topology, geometric analysis, operator algebra, number theory statistics, probability theory and mathematical physics.

We offer
Our new colleagues will become part of an inspirational international research environment with excellent facilities and strong collaborations with a vast international network, research organizations and regulatory stakeholders. We offer a number of positions from which to further develop the mathematical foundations for quantum theory and to combine this pure mathematical initiative with an ambitious build up in the theoretical foundations of quantum field theory and string theory and further in the theoretical foundations of quantum engineering. Given that current development of mathematical foundations of quantum theory draws from and needs a diverse deep understanding of all branches of pure mathematics, we offer a number of positions in all branches of pure mathematics and quantum computer science at QM. We also offer the opportunity to shape our educational programme to benefit from new developments in pedagogical approaches and content.

We expect
The candidates must have a PhD degree in algebra, algebraic geometry, differential geometry, algebraic topology, complex geometry, quantum topology, geometric analysis, operator algebra, number theory, statistic, probability theory, mathematical physics or quantum algorithms, quantum software architecture. 

The candidates must further have an emerging research track in the field and evidence of excellent teaching at minimum undergraduate level (e.g. teaching evaluations). We are seeking highly motivated candidates, who work and communicate well in an international team. The candidates must be able to carry out independent and rigorous work at top international level.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a prerequisite for application. The hired candidate will be offered Danish courses by the university.

Living and working in Odense
Odense is a fast-growing international community with an open Scandinavian culture, affordable housing and living costs.

jobs.occupation: Green Biorefinery Pathways for Carbon Capture and Fiber Valorisation into Biobased Materials
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Green Biorefinery Pathways for Carbon Capture and Fiber Valorisation into Biobased Materials

Research area and project description:
The transition towards a circular bioeconomy requires new technologies that enable the efficient conversion of biomass into high-value products and long-lived carbon-storing materials. This PhD project will investigate how green biorefinery processing and subsequent pretreatment affect the molecular structure and properties of lignocellulosic fibres from grassland biomass.

The PhD is part of the interdisciplinary research project GrassCO2mposites, which aims to develop novel biobased building materials from grass fibres, linking agricultural biomass production, green biorefining and carbon storage in the built environment.

The research will focus on the processing and detailed characterisation of fibre-rich side streams generated during protein extraction in green biorefineries. Different mechanical, chemical and potentially biological pretreatment methods will be investigated to understand and control changes in the composition, molecular organisation and interactions of key structural biopolymers, including cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin.

Advanced analytical methods will be applied to investigate biopolymer composition, molecular structure, crystallinity, fibre morphology and physicochemical properties. The aim is to establish structure–property relationships that can guide the development of processing methods for producing fibres with tailored characteristics suitable for biobased composite materials.

Experimental work will combine laboratory investigations with pilot- and demonstration-scale processing at Aarhus University's green biorefinery facilities. The PhD will collaborate closely with project partners at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Academy on fibre functionalisation, composite development and material performance.

An additional focus will be to strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration with the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University, connecting fundamental biomass processing and biopolymer research with the development and evaluation of biobased construction materials.

The project will contribute new scientific knowledge and scalable processing strategies for the valorisation of agricultural biomass into functional, carbon-storing materials.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants must hold a relevant Master's degree (120 ECTS) in chemical engineering, biotechnology, materials science, polymer science or a closely related discipline.

We seek candidates with a strong academic background in lignocellulosic biomass processing, biorefining, polymer chemistry or biobased materials. Experience with experimental processing and characterisation of biomass-derived fibres and biopolymers is particularly relevant.

Knowledge of analytical techniques such as FTIR, NMR, HPLC, GPC/SEC, DSC, TGA, microscopy, rheology or mechanical testing will be considered an advantage. Experience with cellulose extraction, fibre pretreatment, polymer dissolution or other chemical and physicochemical processing methods is also desirable.

Applicants should have strong experimental and analytical skills, an interest in understanding molecular structure–property relationships, and the ability to plan and conduct independent research.

The project requires an interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across chemical engineering, biotechnology and materials science, including collaboration with researchers working on biobased construction materials.

Good written and spoken English communication skills are required. Experience from relevant research projects or industrial R&D will be considered an advantage.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Hangøvej 2, 8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Associate Professor Morten Ambye-Jensen, e-mail: maj@bce.au.dk (main supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
 
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
 How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 23 November 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 1 February 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
 Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Foundation Models for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
jobs.description:
The Centre for Machine Learning located under the Data Science and Statistics Section of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA) at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a paid PhD research fellowship position within the field of probabilistic machine learning to be filled earliest by 1 March 2027 for a period of three years. 

The research project will investigate new algorithmic principles that make large populations of learning agents solve open-vocabulary control tasks from sparse reward signals. The expected outcomes are new theoretical insights about the algorithmic roots of autonomous behavior and their representative demonstrations in challenging simulation environments. 

IMADA has the unique feature of bringing mathematicians and computer scientists together within a single department to foster theoretically well-backed high-quality data science research. IMADA is home to many ongoing externally funded research projects, as well as to a rich curriculum of data science courses. Data Science and Statistics Group is a synergy platform for the data science experts in IMADA. 

We are seeking candidates with strong desire to make significant contributions to science, specific interest in fundamental machine learning research, and an outstanding theoretical background in probabilistic machine learning and reinforcement learning demonstrated by excellent course grades and by scientific publications at major international peer-reviewed venues of core machine learning research. Strong scientific programming skills demonstrated by contributions to public code repositories or released source code from the candidate’s own publications is a big plus. We also expect excellent spoken and written communication skills in English.

The successful candidate will join the vibrant research atmosphere at the SDU Adaptive Intelligence Laboratory and entertain substantial peer support in both technical and social matters. The candidate will contribute to the publication of high-quality research papers at top-tier machine learning venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, AISTATS, together with the other lab members. The candidate will also fulfill teaching assistantship duties.

We will consider the candidates who have a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics, Statistics, or Theoretical Physics at the time of the commencement of employment. Candidates should demonstrate that they have passed at least two Master’s level courses that cover advanced machine learning topics with a grade that corresponds to top 10% success within the native grade scale.

Place of work
The Department of Mathematics and Computer Science is located at the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, Denmark. The University of Southern Denmark was founded in 1966 and now has more than 27,000 students, almost 20% of whom are from abroad. It has more than 3,800 employees, and 115 different study programmes in the fields of the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. Its main campus is located in Odense, the third largest city in Denmark.

Odense provides family-friendly living conditions with the perfect combination of a historic city centre with an urban feel and yet a close proximity to beaches and recreational areas. Its location on the beautiful island of Funen is ideal with easy access by train or highway to the bigger cities of Aarhus and Copenhagen. As the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen, Denmark’s famous fairytale author, the city is home to a vibrant and creative population that hosts numerous festivals and markets throughout the year.

We recommend that as an international applicant, you take the time to visit Work in Denmark where you will find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark, as well as the International Staff Office at SDU.

jobs.occupation: Warehouse Specialist

Department: Talgo Warranty / Logistics & Warehouse Operations

jobs.occupation: Tenure-track Assistant and Associate Professorships in Algorithms at SDU Vejle
jobs.description:
We seek candidates to join the Algorithms Section at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science and contribute to the development of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and AI in Vejle.
The starting time is negotiable with a preference for Summer 2027. 

The academic environment
Hired candidates will join the Algorithms Section, which spans SDU’s campuses in Odense and Vejle, and become part of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and AI. Based at the new campus in Vejle, in the heart of Denmark’s Triangle Region and its strong and developing IT ecosystem, the centre offers an inclusive, international and collaborative environment for research and education in Computer Science and AI. It connects research, teaching and innovation through collaboration across research groups and with companies, public organizations and international partners.
The Centre for Computer Science and AI at SDU Vejle connects fundamental computer science with AI, data and advanced digital systems. Its shared focus is how architectures, AI, data and advanced algorithms can transform the specification, design, development, validation, deployment and operation of digital systems. The research environment is also home to SustainAI, an international research group advancing the design, development, evolution, testing and operation of sustainable, high-quality and AI-enabled software systems.
We encourage applications from researchers who can complement or strengthen the Algorithms Section while building links to the centre’s wider scientific environment in areas such as data analytics, data science and machine learning; optimization and computational efficiency; programming languages; software engineering and DevOps; AI-driven development and software evolution; and software architectures, cloud-edge computing, and autonomous and agentic systems.

At SDU Vejle, the department is responsible for international BSc and MSc programmes in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. The programmes provide a strong setting for research-based teaching, supervision, and student collaboration with researchers and external partners.

Research profile
We seek candidates with a strong research record in efficient algorithms, broadly understood as spanning algorithm design, analysis and implementation as well as complexity theory. Relevant areas include, but are not limited to, approximation algorithms, combinatorial optimization, cryptology, data structures, fine-grained complexity, experimental algorithmics, and algorithmic research bridging to machine learning and AI.
Scientific excellence is the primary requirement. We particularly welcome candidates in algorithms engineering, optimization, or computational efficiency, whose work combines strong algorithmic foundations with the design, implementation and rigorous evaluation of algorithms for real-world problems.
Each appointment should help create a clear and distinctive identity for the Vejle environment by building critical mass, adding a missing capability, or creating a strong bridge between research areas. Candidates must strengthen at least one core area and connect meaningfully with other parts of the centre through research, education or external collaboration.

Industrial collaboration
Industrial collaboration is a defining theme of the centre. Successful candidates are expected to demonstrate an interest in engaging with companies and public organizations and the potential to contribute to the digital transformation of industry at local, national and international levels. Relevant activities may include collaborative research, industrial PhDs, student collaborations, and experimentation with industrial data and systems.

Qualifications
Successful candidates for a tenure-track assistant professorship must demonstrate a promising research record within the area of the call and some experience with teaching and supervision at BSc or MSc level. They are expected to contribute to research-based teaching, student projects and thesis supervision, including activities that connect students, researchers and external partners.
The Danish tenure-track system provides a focused pathway toward a permanent academic position. Before the end of the sixth year of employment, and contingent upon a positive academic assessment, the Assistant Professor will transition to a tenured Associate Professor position. Read more about SDU’s tenure-track program here.

The evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential. Emphasis will be placed on the ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. 
As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the tenure evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution. 
The evaluation will also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities. 
Successful candidates for an associate professorship must have an international profile, a distinguished research record within the area of the call, and a proven ability to attract third-party funding. Demonstrated success in building and leading research teams, and a strong record of developing and leading research, innovation or industry-engaged activities, will be an advantage. Extensive teaching and supervision experience across BSc and MSc levels is expected.

Application
In addition to the documentation required under SDU’s appointment procedures, applicants should describe:

• 
Possible existing collaboration with industry or public organizations and plans for developing future external partnerships.

• 
How they would collaborate with existing groups in Vejle, supported by concrete examples of potential research, educational or practical collaboration.

Conditions of employment
Appointment as a Tenure Track Assistant Professor is temporary and for an initial up to 6 years period. 
During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

The Danish tenure track employment
The Danish tenure-track employment is a focused assistant professorship with a guaranteed assessment for a permanent position as an associate professor within the tenure-track assistant professor’s field of study.
The head of department will host annual performance- and development reviews, to ensure the progress of the assistant professor’s development towards meeting the qualifications of an associate professorship. A formal midterm evaluation will be conducted by a committee, consisting of the head of the department and two external researchers with relevant qualifications, with the purpose of ensuring the focus of the assistant professor’s activities, as well as to create the basis for the planning of the remaining period.

To qualify for the position as Tenure Track Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD degree by the employment date.

The transition from assistant professor to associate professor
Within the last year of employment, the tenure-track assistant professor is expected to transition into a position as an associate professor position, based on a positive assessment conducted by a formally approved assessment committee, consisting of a chairman appointed by SDU and minimum one external committee member approved by the dean and the academic council.

Successful applicants to tenure-track assistant professor positions must be scholars with an internationally competitive research profile, whose potential is at the forefront of their discipline. The applicants for tenure-track assistant professorships are assessed based on the criteria of the applicant’s potential to reach an international level of scholarly excellence during the tenure-track period. The candidate will only be promoted to associate professor when the assessment committee confirms that the candidate has scholarly merits at a level of international excellence beyond what can normally be expected for associate professors, with reference to the qualification policy of the research group in which the position is announced.
Indicators of relevant scholarly merits could be documented through scholarly output independent of the PhD supervisor, ground-breaking publications, achievement of excellence grants, and international research network.

Application deadline: 31. December 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Organic and Supramolecular Chemistry: Electrically Controlled Cargo Release in [2]Rotaxanes via Mechanochemical Retro Diels-Alder Reactions at SDU in Odense
jobs.description:
A 3-year (5+3) or 4-year (4+4) PhD position in organic and supramolecular chemistry is available for a highly motivated candidate at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy (FKF) at the University of Southern Denmark. The position is funded by a DFF-Research Project 1 grant from the Independent Research Fund Denmark – Natural Sciences and is available from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
The project focuses on the design and synthesis of electroactive molecular machines capable of converting electrically controlled molecular motion into mechanical force. In particular, the project will investigate whether redox-induced shuttling in mechanically interlocked molecules can be used to trigger the cleavage of covalent bonds and thereby enable controlled cargo release.

Project Background
The aim of this project is to develop electrically responsive molecular machines capable of converting redox-induced molecular motion into covalent cargo release.
Specifically, the project will focus on the design and synthesis of [2]rotaxanes incorporating a redox-active monopyrrolotetrathiafulvalene (MPTTF) unit, a cyclobis(paraquat-p-phenylene) (CBPQT4+) macrocycle, and a furan-based unit linked to a cargo molecule through a Diels–Alder adduct.
Upon electrochemical oxidation of the MPTTF unit, the CBPQT4+ macrocycle is expected to undergo shuttling along the molecular axle. The central hypothesis is that this redox-induced motion can generate sufficient mechanical force to promote a retro-Diels–Alder reaction, resulting in the release of the covalently attached cargo molecule. A key objective is to establish a direct mechanistic relationship between redox-induced macrocycle movement, the generation of mechanical force, and the cleavage of a covalent bond.
The project will involve extensive synthetic organic chemistry, the preparation and characterization of mechanically interlocked molecules, and investigations of their electrochemical and mechanical properties using techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, UV–vis spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry.

By combining synthetic, spectroscopic, and electrochemical studies, the project aims to establish whether electrically driven molecular motion can be harnessed to induce covalent bond cleavage. The results are expected to contribute to the fundamental understanding of force transduction in artificial molecular machines and may provide a foundation for future applications in controlled molecular release.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate holds a Master's degree (5+3 programme) or a Bachelor's degree (4+4 programme) in chemistry or a closely related field, preferably with a strong background in synthetic organic chemistry.

The successful candidate should have:

• 
Extensive practical experience in synthetic organic chemistry.

• 
A strong interest in supramolecular chemistry and molecular machines.

• 
Experience with standard analytical and spectroscopic characterization techniques.

• 
The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment.

• 
Good communication skills and proficiency in written and spoken English.

Previous experience in supramolecular chemistry, mechanically interlocked molecules, or tetrathiafulvalene chemistry would be an advantage but is not a prerequisite.
The successful candidate will also be expected to contribute to the supervision of Bachelor's and Master's students working on research projects within the group.

To learn more about the PhD programme at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, read more here. 

Natural Science Research – Interdisciplinary Strength
The Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy is one of four departments at the Faculty of Science, SDU and is located in Odense. At the Department, we contribute to solving some of society’s greatest challenges within energy, environment, health, and sustainability. We succeed because we build bridges between disciplines and transcend traditional boundaries. Our interdisciplinary mindset is not only a fundamental condition, but also our strength. And it is a strength that ensures our research and education are recognized both nationally and internationally.

Our vision is to create and apply knowledge across the natural sciences. We are unique in housing research within physics, chemistry, and pharmacy under one department, which provides excellent opportunities to explore the intersections between these disciplines. Read more about our vision here.

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is based on a collaboration between Novonesis and Aarhus University and is available from 15 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
New model for activated sludge flocculation integrating cellular biochemical reaction potential with the microbial ecology

Research area and project description
While bacterial and activated sludge flocculation is the most important component of wastewater treatment processes, mechanisms governing flocculation are poorly understood. It is difficult to control and optimize activated sludge flocculation, and so downstream clarifiers for removing activated sludge from treated water are overdesigned or overloaded.

Effective flocculation is currently explained in terms of achieving the right balance between good and bad flocculating bacteria. Industrial wastewater treatment plants commonly experience poor flocculating sludges with impaired flocculation, which is attributed to too many bad flocculating bacteria. However, there is in fact a poor correlation between the microbial ecology of industrial wastewater treatment activated sludges and flocculation.
In this project the candidate will build on ongoing research in the host lab demonstrating that biochemical reactions occur within activation sludge that also likely promote flocculation The candidate will establish abiotic and biotic activated sludge models, assess the effect of flocculation stressors characteristic of industrial wastewaters, as well as biological, chemical and mechanical strategies for overcoming these. The research will inform strategies for the industrial to consider to increase the hydraulic of their wastewater treatment plant.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must have a relevant master's degree in biology, biotechnology, biochemistry, biological or chemical engineering or a closely related field.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work will be divided approximately evenly between Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Ole Worms Alle 3, 8000 Aarhus C., Denmark, and Novonesis, Hallas Alle 1, 4400 Kalundborg, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Purchaser, Direct Procurement (12-month parental cover)
jobs.description:
Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial product portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox, mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, and cholera. We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, striving to improve people's health and quality of life worldwide, protecting our tomorrow.

We are seeking a talented Purchaser, Direct Procurement to help ensure a reliable, cost-effective supply of materials that keeps our operations running.

The role involves close collaboration with Global Procurement in Switzerland and extensive cross-functional interaction with Production, Quality, and external suppliers to drive operational excellence and secure reliable supply.

This is a fixed-term parental leave cover position until 31st December 2027.

**About The Team

**You will join a team of eight dedicated purchasing colleagues covering both direct and indirect procurement for our manufacturing site. We operate in a dynamic and fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, making adaptability and collaboration key to success. Quality is at the heart of everything we do, and we take pride in maintaining high standards while ensuring reliable supply to our operations.

As part of the team, you will experience a supportive and collaborative culture where colleagues actively help and learn from each other. We value open communication, mutual respect, and a positive team spirit, and we believe that the best results are achieved when we work together across functions and support one another in meeting both challenges and opportunities.

The role is based in our manufacturing site in Kvistgaard, Denmark and with flexibility for home office (up to 2 days). You will report to the Site Purchasing Manager.

**About The Role

**As a Purchaser within Direct Procurement, you will play a vital role in ensuring the reliable and cost-effective procurement of raw materials to support our operations. This role is hands-on and dynamic, and it offers a unique opportunity to work cross-functionally, build supplier relationships, and contribute to procurement excellence across multiple direct categories.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Issue purchase orders and ensure accurate and timely delivery of goods and services to the site

• Monitor inventory levels and maintain optimal stock levels to support operational continuity

• Identify and mitigate supply disruptions, quality issues, and supplier reliability risks

• Manage procurement activities across direct categories such as consumables, primary and secondary packaging

• Support the end-to-end requisition-to-purchase-order process in Dynamics

• Collaborate with stakeholders to align procurement with operational and business needs

• Evaluate supplier performance in alignment with internal policies

• Contribute to continuous improvement and procurement process standardization

**Qualifications

**To succeed in this role, we imagine you have:

• Experience with direct procurement or purchasing in a manufacturing or operations-driven environment

• Familiarity with ERP/procurement systems (e.g. Dynamics)

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

• Structured, detail-oriented approach with the ability to prioritize in a fast-paced setting

• Full proficiency in Danish and English

**What join Bavarian Nordic?

**You will join an international company with unique technology and colleagues who share a passion for making a difference. As a Purchaser, you will help keep our vaccine production running by ensuring a reliable supply of materials, building strong supplier relationships, and improving day-to-day purchasing processes.

We offer:

• A visible role with an opportunity to make an impact in a collaborative organization

• A supportive team, flexible working conditions, and opportunities to develop your procurement expertise

• A competitive compensation package, pension scheme, health insurance, and bonus opportunities

• A high-quality canteen with a wide selection of meals and take-away options

• Fitness discounts, a massage scheme, and an active staff club offering social and sporting events

**Salary

**Annual base salary range: DKK 530,000 to 620,000 gross

At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to fair and transparent pay. The final base salary within this range will be determined based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and competencies, as well as internal pay equity.

**Caught your interest?

**If you are ready to take on a pivotal role in a growing organization and drive meaningful change in healthcare, apply now and join Bavarian Nordic in our mission to improve health outcomes and foster sustainable growth.

Please note that for this position, we do not support any relocation packages. Candidates must possess a legal basis to work and reside in Denmark.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit _www.bavarian-nordic.com
